boards.title: Your First Weekend at Indiana Wesleyan University-Marion, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A conservative Friday-to-Sunday sequence combining IWU landmarks, student facilities, recreation, arts, and two public Marion destinations.

cards.title: Start at the Campus Hub
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival · Barnes Student Center
cards.notes: Begin at Barnes to locate dining, student services, the post office, campus store, theater, and everyday gathering areas.
cards.short_summary: Use IWU’s central community building to get oriented before exploring farther.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU identifies Barnes Student Center as the Marion campus community center and lists dining, student services, a theater, post office, and campus store inside.
cards.access_notes: Building and individual service access may vary; consult posted campus hours after arrival.

cards.title: Take a Quiet Reset
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Williams Prayer Chapel
cards.notes: Pause for personal prayer or reflection, then photograph the chapel exterior without interrupting anyone using the sanctuary.
cards.short_summary: A reflective first stop introduces the spiritual side of the Marion campus.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU describes Williams Prayer Chapel as a sanctuary for personal prayer, reflection, and meditation and features it among the Marion campus highlights.
cards.access_notes: Interior access hours are not published on the cited page; respect services, private reflection, and posted restrictions.

cards.title: Settle In Over Dinner
cards.subtitle: Friday dinner · Baldwin Dining Commons
cards.notes: Meet a classmate for dinner and scan the labeled stations before choosing among the grill, pizza, salad, vegetarian, or allergen-free options.
cards.short_summary: A practical first meal helps newcomers learn how campus dining is organized.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU states that Baldwin Dining Commons is inside Barnes Student Center, serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner daily, and provides multiple food stations.
cards.source_title: Life on Campus in a Christ-centered Community
cards.access_notes: Meal periods and entry rules can vary; confirm current student dining hours and bring the required meal credential or payment.

cards.title: Learn the Recreation Setup
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Recreation and Wellness Center
cards.notes: Tour the available fitness areas with a friend, note equipment rules, and ask staff which pool, track, or gym sessions fit your schedule.
cards.short_summary: An early walkthrough makes future recreation plans easier and more specific.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU says the Recreation and Wellness Center contains gymnasiums, a natatorium, racquetball courts, weight and fitness rooms, an elevated track, and locker facilities.
cards.access_notes: No current weekend hours are stated on the cited page; verify student eligibility, posted hours, and activity-specific rules.

cards.title: Find Your First Study Base
cards.subtitle: Saturday late morning · Jackson Library
cards.notes: Walk the building, locate a comfortable workstation, and bookmark the library tools you expect to use during your first assignments.
cards.short_summary: A low-pressure library visit turns an unfamiliar academic resource into a usable base.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU describes Jackson Library as a 79,000-square-foot facility with campus-network connections throughout and identifies Saturday hours as 11 a.m.–8 p.m. in its 2025–2026 handbook.
cards.source_title: 2025–2026 Student Handbook | School of Integrated Health
cards.access_notes: The cited 2025–2026 handbook lists Saturday hours of 11 a.m.–8 p.m.; confirm the live hours page for holidays or academic-break changes.

cards.title: Photograph the Historic Anchor
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · John Wesley Administration Building
cards.notes: Use the self-guided campus map to approach the restored exterior, take a daylight photo, and compare it with newer campus architecture.
cards.short_summary: The oldest surviving campus building provides a clear visual link to IWU’s past.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU states that the John Wesley Administration Building opened in 1894, is the only remaining building from the original campus, and was renovated in 2003.
cards.access_notes: Plan this as an exterior stop; offices and interior spaces may be closed or restricted on weekends.

cards.title: Check the Campus Stage Calendar
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Phillippe Performing Arts Center
cards.notes: Look over the current onStage listings with friends and choose a future concert, recital, or play that fits everyone’s calendar and budget.
cards.short_summary: A calendar check introduces IWU’s recurring music and theater options without assuming a show that weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU’s onStage series presents Music Division concerts, Theatre Guild plays, and visiting artists at venues inside the Phillippe Performing Arts Center.
cards.access_notes: Lobby and auditorium access depend on scheduled events; consult the current listing and obtain a ticket when required.

cards.title: Make a Garden Photo Loop
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · The Gardens of Matter Park
cards.notes: Walk through the planted garden and Meadow on foot, pause at the bronze statues and butterfly garden, and follow every posted park rule.
cards.short_summary: This public garden adds a visually varied off-campus stop to the first weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Marion says the 6.3-acre Gardens and Meadow contain more than 7,000 annual plants, shade structures, bronze statues, seating, and a butterfly garden.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access is subject to posted park conditions and private events; bicycles and skating are prohibited within the Gardens.

cards.title: Follow the River Through Marion
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Mississinewa Riverwalk
cards.notes: Choose a manageable out-and-back section, bring water, stay on the paved route, and turn around early enough to return before dark.
cards.short_summary: A measured river walk offers movement and a first look at Marion beyond campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Marion identifies the Mississinewa Riverwalk as a 2.25-mile paved recreation path running from Washington Street Bridge to Matter Park’s fishing pond.
cards.access_notes: The official page does not publish operating hours; use daylight, remain on the maintained path, and follow current park notices.

cards.title: Close the Weekend With a Plan
cards.subtitle: Sunday night · Center Hall
cards.notes: Bring your syllabus and calendar, identify the week’s fixed commitments, and leave with one short task list for Monday morning.
cards.short_summary: A final planning session converts the weekend’s orientation into an actionable first week.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU’s current instructional-facilities catalog states that Center Hall contains general-purpose classrooms and a 24-7 Study Room.
cards.access_notes: The catalog identifies a 24-7 Study Room; verify student-ID access, building entry instructions, and any temporary closure notices.

warnings: Weekend and interior-access details are not published for several campus facilities; those cards explicitly direct students to verify posted hours or event access.
Coordinates and entity-specific map URLs were left null because they could not be verified from the cited direct sources.
